findings.governingReading: Shirou hears a splashing, surging sound like blood flowing.
findings.explanation: The English turns the simile into an assertion that the audible substance is blood.

findings.highlight: My vocal organs appeal to me about the pain.
findings.evidenceJa: 発声器官は俺のモノではなくなったように、耐え難い痛みをひたすらに訴える。
findings.governingReading: As though no longer belonging to Shirou, his vocal organs do nothing but cry out the unbearable pain.
findings.explanation: The English awkwardly makes the organs appeal to Shirou and omits bodily alienation, intolerability, and relentless expression.

findings.highlight: if there’s a wound this big
findings.evidenceJa: 肘の先からまるごと、バケツめいた孔が出来たら
findings.governingReading: A bucket-like hole has taken away the arm wholesale beyond the elbow.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the exact catastrophic anatomy and bucket image to a generically large wound.

findings.highlight: To make you use your Command Spell
findings.evidenceJa: 貴方に令呪を使わせるこの狩りの中で
findings.governingReading: Within this hunt designed to force Shirou to use a Command Spell, Rider set herself conditions.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the objective but omits Rider’s explicit framing of the encounter as a hunt.

findings.highlight: Saber. I… have… to call… Saber
findings.evidenceJa: セイバー。俺は、セイバーを、呼ばない、と
findings.governingReading: Shirou forms the decision that he will not call Saber, despite dying suspended in the trap.
findings.explanation: The English reverses refusal into obligation, erasing the defining choice not to compel Saber and changing the death branch’s characterization and causal meaning.

findings.highlight: I have to call for Saber… with my Command Spell…
findings.governingReading: Through the Command Spell, Saber…; Shirou’s cognition fails on an unfinished object marker before he can complete the thought.
findings.explanation: The English supplies a coherent obligation and completed action, removing the syntactic collapse that distinguishes this dying thought from a resolved command.

findings.evidenceJa: 胸を抉って息の根を止めますが
findings.governingReading: Rider says she would gouge open Shirou’s chest in order to stop his breath and end his life.
findings.explanation: Even the closer conditional branch omits the attack’s explicitly stated lethal purpose, leaving only mutilation.

findings.highlight: your brain will not function even if you are saved.
findings.evidenceJa: もう脳はまともに機能しないでしょうね
findings.governingReading: Rider predicts that Shirou’s brain will probably no longer function normally or properly even if he survives.
findings.explanation: The English omits まともに and strengthens the prediction into categorical total nonfunction.
